discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body systems with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Feynman's idea of simulating quantum physics with controllable quantum systems became a laboratory reality through ultracold atoms in optical lattices. Peter Zoller provided the theoretical blueprint, showing that atoms in optical lattices realize Hubbard models with tunable parameters and laying out how to engineer and probe strongly correlated phases. Immanuel Bloch and Markus Greiner achieved the landmark observation of the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition (2002), and subsequently developed quantum gas microscopes resolving and controlling individual atoms in lattices. This programme opened a new field: the study of antiferromagnetism, many-body localization, topological bands, gauge fields and non-equilibrium dynamics in regimes beyond classical computation. It has transformed how condensed-matter questions are posed and answered, and it is the most mature realization of analog quantum simulation, now a central pillar of quantum science worldwide.
